subject: Capacity gap analysis & pricing sensitivity for HyperOps commitment
messages:
From: Alex Liu <alex@hyperops.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops-team@hyperops.ai
Date: 2028-07-02T08:12:00Z
Subject: Quick capsule: expected traffic pattern + a weird burst window

Evelyn —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We sketched a rough forecast internally and noticed a couple of potential gaps when mapping to the Reserved Capacity options you shared. High level:
- Baseline concurrency: ~420 active sessions during US business hours
- Peak burst: intermittent spikes up to ~2,200 simultaneous sessions for 8–12 minutes during product releases (twice/month)
- Prompt/response sizes: median prompt 650 tokens, median response 270 tokens; tail responses up to 2,500 tokens (rare)

I attached our token mix snapshot. Can you help translate this into a practical capacity gap analysis and show how pricing changes if we shift more traffic to burst credits vs committing higher base capacity?

Also — are there guardrails we should set to avoid OOMs when the rare long responses hit multiple GPUs?

Cheers,
Alex
VP Engineering, HyperOps

Attachments: HyperOps_token_mix.csv (CSV, 38KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Liu <alex@hyperops.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T12:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick capsule: expected traffic pattern + a weird burst window

Alex — thanks for the detail and the token mix. This is exactly what we need to do a proper sizing + pricing sensitivity. Immediate notes:
- Baseline of 420 concurrent sessions maps to X GPUs depending on model selection and batching. We’ll run a matrix for the two model families you tried in staging (gpt-medium-ish open model, and a more compact quantized variant).
- Bursts to 2.2k are the cost driver; we typically model these as a short-term autoscale + reserved burst pool rather than permanently committing to 5x baseline.
- For rare 2.5k-token responses we’ll recommend a session-level fallback policy (stream early cutoff + fallback to a higher-memory variant) and prefix KV caching for repeated user context.

I’ll ask Marissa to produce a capacity gap table and Ben to sketch the pricing scenarios (commit vs burst credits). Karthik, please weigh in on safe memory thresholds for long-tail responses.

Next step: we’ll follow up with a short workbook that shows (1) suggested reserved base fleet, (2) burst pool sizing, (3) monthly cost across three commitment tiers. Will share by EOD Tuesday.

—Evelyn
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: ops-capacity-gap-diagram.png (PNG, 240KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Liu <alex@hyperops.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-03T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick capsule: expected traffic pattern + a weird burst window

Alex — attaching the gap workbook and a matrix view. Highlights in the workbook:
- Baseline recommendation: 12 GPUs (A100-class equivalence) for the compact model variant to comfortably cover 420 concurrent sessions with p95 latency < 350ms.
- Burst pool recommendation: 18 GPUs on pre-warmed burst instances to handle 2.2k peak (with staged autoscale), yields p99 latency target ~1.2s under designed batching.
- Tail responses (2.5k tokens): reserve 2-3 high-memory slots (bigger VN-GPUs or pinned higher-memory model variants) and a safety circuit to stop oversized requests from saturating the pooled KV cache.

I added a sheet called 'pricing-sensitivity' that toggles committed base size vs burst credits. See the three scenarios: Conservative commit, Hybrid (moderate commit + burst credits), and Aggressive burst-only.

Let us know if you want a scenario where we quantize models further to trade compute for small quality delta — that reduces GPU needs significantly.

Attachments: commitment_pricing_scenarios.xlsx (XLSX, 84KB)

- Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Liu <alex@hyperops.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-04T14:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick capsule: expected traffic pattern + a weird burst window

Alex — quick commercial sketch to go with Marissa's workbook:
- Conservative commit (12 GPUs): baseline cost $38k/month; burst credits priced at $0.48/token-equivalent for on-demand scaling; expected monthly overage if bursts occur twice/month as you described ~ $12k additional.
- Hybrid (8 GPUs commit + 10 GPU burst pool): baseline cost $28k/month + burst pool reserved at lower hourly rate for the 10 GPUs; effective blended cost (~3% lower) but increases operational complexity for predictable bursts.
- Burst-only (0 GPUs commit): higher unit cost during peaks; good if you want zero upfront commit but loses price predictability.

If the long-tail 2.5k-token events are business-critical, recommend adding a small reserved high-memory pool (2 GPUs) to avoid expensive on-demand failures and to maintain SLOs. That adds ~$6k/month but lowers p99 failure risk by ~90%.

Happy to walkthrough line by line on a call.

—Ben
Head of Pre-Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is super helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs before we present to finance next week: 
1) If we choose the Hybrid option, what is the expected cold-start time when the burst pool scales from 10 -> 18 GPUs? Is there a way to keep a small number warm to guarantee < 30s ramp for the first batch?
2) What operational tooling do you provide to let us observe per-route token spend and enforce per-customer caps inside our account?

Also — we want to run a 2-week pilot in staging to validate the quantized model option. Can you give us a quick checklist for what telemetry we should capture to compare quality vs cost?

Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Liu <alex@hyperops.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-06T15:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick capsule: expected traffic pattern + a weird burst window

Alex — quick answers inline:
1) Burst cold-start: with pre-warmed placeholders we can bring extra GPUs to readiness in ~18–45s depending on cloud region and instance mix; to guarantee < 30s we recommend keeping 2–4 pre-warmed workers in the burst pool (small hourly cost).
2) Observability: Redwood Console exposes per-route token-level breakdowns, per-model spend, and alerting for per-customer caps. We can provision a dashboard and a webhook to your billing system.

Pilot telemetry checklist (2-week staging pilot):
- Capture per-request: prompt tokens, response tokens, latency, model variant, GPU id, queue wait time.
- Failure/error logs: OOMs, retries, eviction events.
- Quality sampling: 200 labeled prompts pre/post quantization to compute BLEU/ROUGE or a simple acceptance % from product QA.
- Cost telemetry: tokens-attributed-to-route and effective GPU-hours by model variant.

Karthik
Principals, Inference Engineering, Redwood Inference
